paragraphs.text: Parkinson disease-8 (PARK8) is an autosomal dominant form of parkinsonism. Its clinical features closely resemble those of idiopathic Parkinson disease (PD): levodopa-responsive bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, and impaired postural reflexes, with slow progression. The neuropathology varies, even within a single family. Affected individuals consistently show nigral degeneration, which may be accompanied by brainstem or diffuse Lewy bodies, by tau-positive neurofibrillary tangles, or by neither.

checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant parkinsonism associated with variable synuclein and tau pathology.
checks.explanation: Title describes autosomal dominant parkinsonism; abstract notes linkage to PARK8.

checks.evidence_quote: Lewy bodies (LB) limited to brainstem nuclei were detected in one case, diffuse LB in the second, neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) without LB in the third, and neither NFT nor LB in the fourth.

paragraphs.text: Wszolek et al. (1995) described family D, a western Nebraska kindred whose ancestors probably came from England. The pedigree spanned 6 generations and contained 188 individuals, 18 of them affected. Affected members developed typical levodopa-responsive PD with bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, and impaired postural reflexes. Eye movement abnormalities, pyramidal and cerebellar signs, sensory disturbances, and orthostatic blood pressure changes did not occur, and the disease progressed slowly. In 1 affected individual, [18F]-6-fluoro-L-dopa PET showed decreased uptake in a pattern consistent with PD. Autopsy of another affected individual showed neuronal and pigment loss, gliosis, and Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra pars compacta. The authors concluded that the disorder closely resembled, if it was not identical to, idiopathic PD.

paragraphs.text: Saunders-Pullman et al. (2011) used the UPSIT to compare 31 PD patients carrying LRRK2 G2019S with 30 PD patients without the mutation and 46 controls. Olfaction in the G2019S PD patients was impaired compared with controls but less impaired than in non-LRRK2 PD patients (difference = 6.13, p = 0.0012).
